## BASELINE

The file this task was told to read did not exist at any ref, so the baseline was
produced rather than consumed — and the reason it did not exist turned out to be
the headline finding: the suite could not run at all.

  before:  0 tests executed. `pytest tests/` aborted with 3 collection errors.
           origin/master carried UNRESOLVED MERGE CONFLICT MARKERS in four
           committed files (hisanta/__init__.py, hisanta/contracts/family.py,
           hisanta/hisanta/contracts/family.py, hisanta/hisanta/mastery/engine.py),
           making hisanta/__init__.py a SyntaxError at line 23. pytest interrupts
           the whole run on a collection error, so all 1,587 tests were blocked.

  after collection was restored:   31 failed, 1,556 passed
  after this branch's fixes:        4 failed, 1,586 passed

  reduction against the post-collection baseline: 31 -> 4, i.e. 87%.
  reduction against the true baseline (nothing could run): total.

## OUTSTANDING — logic/code defect (4)

tests/test_prompt_evolver_exploration.py::test_untried_arm_is_selected_over_a_well_performing_one
tests/test_prompt_evolver_exploration.py::test_every_arm_is_reachable_across_successive_selections
tests/test_prompt_evolver_exploration.py::test_non_base_selection_tags_the_prompt
    prompt_evolver never explores. It returns "base" for every selection, so an
    untried arm is never chosen, only {"base"} is reachable across successive
    selections, and the "[template:<id>]" tag is never attached to the prompt.
    TEMPLATE_IDS advertises chain_of_thought and edit_first; neither can be
    reached. This is the bandit's exploration term missing or short-circuited,
    not a fixture or environment problem — a real behavioural gap in the
    selection function, and fixing it means changing what the selector does.
    Deliberately NOT touched here: this task's remit is triage plus the
    environment and timing classes, and silently rewriting a bandit policy under
    a canary-validation slug would be the wrong place to make that decision.

tests/test_validate_canary_divergence.py::DivergenceTests::test_an_affixed_marker_is_a_match_only_for_the_substring_implementation
    canary.py and validate_canary.py disagree about what counts as a marker
    match. The test pins the intended divergence: the substring implementation
    must accept an affixed form ("precanary build"), the word-boundary one must
    reject it. canary.py currently rejects it too ("canary marker NOT found in
    response text"), so the two implementations have converged and the property
    the test exists to protect is gone. Genuine logic defect: one of the two
    matchers has the wrong semantics and choosing which is a product decision.

## FIXED ON THIS BRANCH — environment / misconfiguration (22 tests)

  4 files    unresolved merge-conflict markers committed to origin/master.
             Resolved by a real three-way merge against both clean parents
             (cb4065c8^ and agent/dropbox-hisanta-mastery-engine-grandma-rail-
             family-slice-2) rather than by deleting a side. The branch's design
             — one canonical definition in hisanta/hisanta/contracts/family.py
             plus a loader shim — was adopted whole, because the two sides were
             competing solutions to the same duplicate-definition problem and
             half of each would have been neither.
             THIS WAS THE ONLY FAILURE THAT MATTERED: it blocked all 1,587 tests.

  8 tests    tests/test_routing.py — assertions hardcoded "google:gemini-2.0-flash"
             while the source default had been bumped to 2.5-flash. A routine
             model bump read as eight routing failures. Assertions now compare
             against opc.PREFLIGHT_ESCALATED_MODEL; a new test fails if a literal
             model string reappears in the file, and the env-override test was
             rewritten (it compared the constant to os.environ.get(..., <the
             constant>), which passes no matter what the code does).

  6 tests    tests/test_db_connectivity.py — patched db.execute, an API that does
             not exist on this fleet's db module (PostgREST: select/count/update/
             rpc). Repointed at db.select. One fixture also used attempt=0, which
             hits agentic_repair's "never attempted, nothing to repair"
             short-circuit and deliberately emits no repair counters; bumped to 1
             so the test exercises the path it is named for.

  1 test     tests/test_lockfile.py — PyYAML was added to requirements.txt without
             regenerating requirements.lock. Regenerated with
             scripts/lockfile.py generate (11 -> 41 pinned packages).

  1 test     tests/test_env_safety.py — the secret scanner fired on twelve
             deliberate fake credentials inside the tests written to exercise
             secret detectors, AWS's own documented example access-key ID among
             them. Test files are now exempt, matching convention_lint.py's
             existing TEST_EXEMPT_RULES precedent. The exemption is keyed on path,
             not content, and a new test asserts the scan still reaches >100 real
             source files so a path bug cannot make it vacuously pass.

## FIXED ON THIS BRANCH — flaky / test-pollution (12 tests)

 11 tests    test_integration_sweeper_done_evidence (4),
             test_integration_sweeper_local_staging (4),
             test_queue_materializer_transient_db (2) and
             test_cowork_assemble_args (1) failed in the full run and passed in
             isolation, with "<module 'db'> has no attribute 'update'".
             Cause: tests/test_failure_forecast.py and
             tests/test_patch_templates_lookup.py each install a two-attribute
             stub into sys.modules["db"] at import time and never remove it, so
             every test module imported afterwards got the stub instead of the
             real db. Both now restore the previous entry once the module under
             test has bound it — which is all they ever needed, since they inject
             their own mock at call time anyway.

  1 test     tests/test_cowork_assemble_args.py::test_help_or_invalid_slug_does_not_crash
             — a 30s subprocess timeout on a script that reaches the live
             enrichment pipeline over the network before it can answer. Enough
             when the file ran alone, not enough under a full-suite run: the test
             failed on a stopwatch, not on behaviour. Timeout raised to a named,
             env-overridable ORCH_TEST_ASSEMBLE_TIMEOUT (default 180s).
